subject.title: Suppress model fallback notices in rooms

question: Should fallback notices remain visible in private/direct conversations but be hidden in every group and channel room, or should visibility follow a more explicit operator-versus-external delivery policy?
rationale: Current behavior intentionally exposes fallback transitions for observability, while this PR changes that default based solely on chat type; source inspection cannot determine which shared rooms are trusted operator surfaces or whether direct external chats must also suppress the diagnostics.

options.title: Use a surface-aware policy
options.body: Preserve lifecycle events everywhere and deliver notices only on explicitly private or operator-facing surfaces rather than treating `ChatType` as the complete trust boundary.

options.title: Adopt room-only suppression
options.body: Suppress notices in all group and channel rooms, retain direct-chat notices, and explicitly accept that trusted operator rooms lose the messages.

options.title: Keep current visibility
options.body: Do not merge the suppression behavior and continue relying on existing source-suppression metadata and operational guidance.

recommendation.title: Use a surface-aware policy
recommendation.body: Preserve lifecycle events everywhere and deliver notices only on explicitly private or operator-facing surfaces rather than treating `ChatType` as the complete trust boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They substantially integrated the original fallback-observability feature and are the strongest available history signal for deciding its intended visibility boundary.
